headline: Highest risk is A→B prompt/data misuse via A’s broad egress and MCP/API integrations; B is local-only, so most pairwise harms are limited but not absent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can ingest and emit content through APIs/MCP, and its tool-use pattern includes direct function calls or an MCP server. godot_rl_agents has no documented input channel, so a direct bridge is not shown; however, if A’s outputs are copied into B’s prompts or environment, injected instructions could propagate. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF A’s output is pasted into B’s prompt or config files
IF a shared MCP server or message queue is introduced between the agents
mitigations: Disable any copy-paste bridge between A and B
Strip instructions from A’s outputs before reuse
Run B with a fixed, non-editable prompt template
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to A outputs
requires-engineering: isolate any shared MCP or queue channel

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data and has broad network egress, but godot_rl_agents shows no data classes touched and no I/O surfaces. With no shared workspace or documented data path, leakage from B is not evidenced; the main risk is accidental exposure if A’s sensitive outputs are manually forwarded into B.
conditions: IF both agents are placed in the same shared workspace
IF A’s CRM/email/calendar data is exported into B’s inputs
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces
Do not route CRM or email exports into B
Review A’s outbound API destinations
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation
requires-engineering: add DLP checks on any shared files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and broad API/network activity, while godot_rl_agents is not runnable and has no documented write surfaces. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable resources or shared locks, so direct capability conflict is unlikely; uncertainty remains because A’s integrations could still collide with external services if co-scheduled.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same external API account
IF A is run in multiple instances against the same CRM or calendar
mitigations: Avoid sharing writable API credentials
Run only one A instance per external account
Schedule writes outside overlapping windows
requires-engineering: add resource locks for shared APIs
requires-engineering: separate OAuth principals per agent

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions, and godot_rl_agents could consume A’s outputs if an operator wires them together. B has no documented verification or action-taking safeguards, so A’s mistaken facts could cascade into downstream game or workflow decisions. The interaction is inferred rather than documented, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF B is configured to treat A’s text as authoritative input
IF A’s outputs are used to trigger downstream actions without human review
mitigations: Require human review before acting on A outputs
Add a verification step in B’s pipeline
Limit A outputs to structured fields only
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating
requires-engineering: log and diff A-to-B handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles CRM, email, calendar, and support data with broad egress, which can create retention or residency issues if paired with a stricter downstream workflow. godot_rl_agents shows no data handling obligations, so the compliance concern is mainly A-side; however, if A’s regulated data is forwarded into B-linked storage or logs, policy mismatch becomes plausible.
conditions: IF regulated customer data from A is copied into B-linked logs or storage
IF A’s outbound APIs are subject to a stricter residency or retention policy than B’s handling
mitigations: Do not forward regulated data into B logs
Set short retention on A exports
Review outbound destinations for residency
requires-engineering: add retention controls per data class
requires-engineering: document a shared DPA and deletion workflow
